artworks.title: Las Hilanderas (The Fable of Arachne)
artworks.description: Velázquez's Prado masterpiece folds Arachne's contest with Athena into a tapestry workshop — in the background the Lydian weaver's challenge becomes art about art itself.

artworks.title: Pallas and Arachne
artworks.description: Rubens paints Athena's fury as Arachne's loom is struck — the mortal weaver's pride met by the goddess who will turn her into a spider.

artworks.title: Minerva and Arachne
artworks.description: Houasse's Versailles canvas from the Story of Minerva cycle shows the goddess confronting Arachne at her loom — the weaving contest as court allegory of skill and hubris.

popCulture.title: Las Hilanderas
popCulture.creator: Diego Velázquez
popCulture.description: Velázquez's Prado canvas folds Arachne's contest into a tapestry workshop — Athena's wrath as Baroque meta-painting.

popCulture.title: Arachne
popCulture.description: The Lydian weaver turned spider remains the emblem of craft that rivals the gods — and of arachnid etymology itself.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Supergiant's sequel brings Arachne into Melinoë's path — the spider-woman as ally and reminder of Athena's curse.
